judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: Top-level desktop menu item "Ações Afirmativas" with href="#". It is not a link to a page: the theme's controller.js prevents the default action on click and toggles the item's submenu (setting aria-expanded), and hover opens it too. Its purpose is to open the Ações Afirmativas submenu, and its text names that submenu; its own list item holds the nested list (Acessibilidade, Comunidades Tradicionais, LGBTQIAPN+, Mulheres, Negros), which is programmatically determined context. So the claim that nothing around it tells its purpose is false of the capture, which gave the model that list item text. The live page has the same markup. Using a link with href="#" as a disclosure is a 4.1.2 role matter at most, not a 2.4.4 failure. The model had the context and judged wrongly.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The site search field in the header (input#s, no label element, placeholder "Busca", next to a magnifier submit button). Its only label is the placeholder "Busca" (Search). 2.4.6 asks that labels describe topic or purpose; "Busca" on a header search box states its purpose, and that tells users to enter what they want to search for, so the claim is not true of it. Demanding that the label spell out what to enter asks for instructions (a 3.3.2-style requirement), which is more than 2.4.6 requires. Other problems here belong to other criteria: the placeholder's 3.03:1 contrast (1.4.3) and the unnamed icon button (4.1.2, a different element). The live page has the same field.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Placeholder "Busca" in the header search field. The theme's live style.css sets input[type=text] color to --cor-texto-medio #949494 and ::placeholder to inherit (and #949494 on focus), with no background, so it sits on white; the screenshot's darkest glyph pixels are exactly #949494 on #ffffff, 3.03:1, at 14px normal weight (the 801-1420px media query sets --fonte-pequena to 14px), so 4.5:1 applies. Skeptic checks: the placeholder is the field's only visible label, so it is information-bearing text and no 1.4.3 exception (incidental, logotype, large text) applies. The page offers an "Alto Contraste" toggle that turns the field white on black, but G174 holds only if the alternate version conforms to all success criteria, and the same DOM in that mode keeps failures such as the alt="Imagem da página" images (1.1.1), so it does not rescue the default presentation. The capture matches the live CSS. The claim names the failure.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: Top-level item "Vida Acadêmica" in the off-canvas mobile menu (#menu-overlay, moved off screen with right:-100% but still exposed to assistive technology), linking to https://www.ufpb.br/vida-academica/. That address is the archive of the "Vida Acadêmica Sem Dúvidas" series: heading "Postagens / Vida Acadêmica Sem Dúvidas" and a list of explainers about student life (institutional e-mail, student policy, internships, CRA, where to eat, academic centres). Its <title> is just the latest post's title, as captured, so the claim's sentence is true of the capture. But the link text "Vida Acadêmica" (academic life) does describe what the destination offers; Understanding 2.4.4 does not require the destination's name, and the odd <title> is the destination's own 2.4.2 matter. No other link shares the name and leads elsewhere (the desktop "Vida Acadêmica" has the same href). The live page matches. The model read the archive's latest-post <title> as the page's identity and judged wrongly, though it also had the heading.
